title: ACT ON SPECIAL MEASURES FOR RESTORATION REGISTRATION AND PRESERVATION REGISTRATION OF LAND WITH UNRESTORED OWNERSHIP REGISTRATION IN RECOVERED AREAS
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to promote the registration of restoration of ownership for land with unrestored ownership registration within recovered areas, and to enable the registration of real estate, which is required to be registered under the Registration of Real Estate Act but for which no registration of preservation of ownership has been made or the entries in the register do not coincide with the actual legal relationship, through simplified procedures, thereby contributing to efficient land management and the protection of real estate ownership in recovered areas.

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
  1. "Recovered areas" means the recovered districts north of 38 degrees north latitude (including areas south of 38 degrees north latitude incorporated into the administrative districts of the same districts) and the areas of Jangdan-myeon, Gunnae-myeon, Jinseo-myeon, and Jindong-myeon in Paju-gun, Gyeonggi-do;
  2. "Competent authority" means the head of a Si/Gun who manages the cadastral records within the recovered areas;
  3. “Land with unrestored ownership registration” means land for which, since the cadastral records were wholly or partially destroyed or lost prior to July 27, 1953, matters concerning land indication have been restored and registered in the land register or the forest land register; but matters concerning ownership have not been restored and registered.

Article 3 (Scope of application) This Act applies to real estate in recovered areas; provided, this Act shall not apply to areas north of the Southern Boundary Demarcation Line determined under the armistice agreement commonly known as the Korean Armistice Agreement that entered into force on July 27, 1953, or to real estate for which litigation concerning the attribution of ownership is pending before a court. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1988>

CHAPTER II REGISTRATION FOR RESTORATION OF OWNERSHIP

Article 4 (Application for registration of restoration of ownership) (1) An owner of land with unrestored ownership registration (including heirs, de facto assignees, and other de facto owners) may apply for the registration of restoration of ownership to the competent authority, along with documents proving that he or she is the owner as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) In cases under paragraph (1), if documents proving that he or she is the owner cannot be obtained, a written guarantee signed by at least 3 guarantors shall be submitted.

Article 5 (Qualifications and appointment of guarantors) (1) A person eligible to be a guarantor under Article 4(2) shall be a person who resided in the relevant Ri/Dong as an adult for at least 1 year between August 15, 1945, and July 27, 1953, has a history of residing in the relevant Ri/Dong for at least 7 years, and currently resides in the relevant Ri/Dong where residents reside at all times in the Ri/Dong where the land is located, or a person who resided in the relevant Ri/Dong as an adult for at least 1 year between August 15, 1945, and July 27, 1953, has a history of residing in the relevant Ri/Dong or an adjacent Ri/Dong for at least 5 years, and currently resides in the relevant Ri/Dong or an adjacent Ri/Dong where residents do not reside at all times in the Ri/Dong where the land is located, and who in either case does not fall under any ground for disqualification prescribed by Presidential Decree; in such cases, the scope of adjacent Ri/Dong shall be determined and publicly notified by the competent head of a Si/Gun. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1988>
  (2) Up to 5 guarantors for each Ri/Dong shall be appointed by the head of a Si/Eup/Myeon for Ri/Dong areas where residents reside at all times, and by the head of a Si/Gun for Ri/Dong areas where residents do not reside at all times; provided, matters concerning the procedures for appointment and dismissal of guarantors and the procedures for issuing written guarantees shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) When the head of a Si/Gun or the head of an Eup/Myeon appoints a guarantor, he or she shall conduct a rigorous investigation in advance into the candidate's history of residence, existence of grounds for disqualification, and the degree of trust from neighboring residents.

Article 6 (Establishment and functions of Land Owner Restoration Examination Committee) (1) To examine and decide matters concerning applications for the registration of restoration of ownership for land within recovered areas, a Land Owner Restoration Examination Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Si/Gun Committee") shall be established in the Si/Gun having jurisdiction over the relevant land, and a Land Owner Restoration Re-examination Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Do Committee") shall be established in the Do.
  (2) The Si/Gun Committee shall examine and decide matters concerning applications for the registration of restoration of ownership, and the Do Committee shall re-examine and decide matters concerning objections to the decisions made by the Si/Gun Committee.

Article 7 (Composition of committees) (1) Each committee shall be composed of not more than 7 members, including 1 chairperson and 1 vice-chairperson.
  (2) A Si/Gun Committee shall be composed of the following persons; provided, the members under subparagraph 4 shall perform their duties as members only for land within the jurisdiction of the relevant Eup/Myeon/Dong:
  1. One prosecutor of a district public prosecutors' office or a branch office designated by the chief prosecutor of the competent district public prosecutors' office;
  2. The chief of the competent police station;
  3. The head of the department in charge of cadastral matters and the head of the department in charge of farmland of the competent Si/Gun;
  4. The head of the competent Eup/Myeon/Dong (limited to the head of a Dong in a Si; hereinafter the same shall apply);
  5. Not more than 2 persons appointed by the head of a Si/Gun from among attorneys-at-law or other persons with extensive knowledge and experience.
  (3) A Do Committee shall be composed of the following persons:
  1. One judge of a district court or a branch court designated by the chief judge of the district court located in the relevant Do;
  2. One prosecutor of a district public prosecutors' office or a branch office designated by the chief prosecutor of the district public prosecutors' office located in the relevant Do;
  3. The director of the bureau in charge of cadastral matters and the director of the bureau in charge of farmland of the Do;
  4. Not more than 3 persons appointed by the Do Governor from among attorneys-at-law or other persons with extensive knowledge and experience.
  (4) The chairperson and the vice-chairperson shall be elected from among the members of the committee by mutual vote; provided, the chairperson shall be qualified as an attorney-at-law.
  (5) Matters necessary for meetings and other operations of each committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 8 (Public announcement, objections, and referral for examination) (1) Upon receipt of an application for the registration of restoration of ownership, the competent authority shall, without delay, make a public announcement of the matters prescribed by Presidential Decree for 3 months on the bulletin boards of the relevant Si/Gun/Eup/Myeon and Ri/Dong offices (including adjacent Ri/Dong referred to in the latter part of Article 5(1)) and publish such announcement at least once in a daily newspaper; and shall conduct a factual investigation into the current status of possession and use of the relevant land, the existence of disputes concerning ownership, and documents related to proof of ownership.
  (2) Upon expiration of the period of public announcement, the competent authority shall, without delay, refer the application for the registration of restoration of ownership, any objections filed within such period, and the factual investigation materials under paragraph (1), along with other reference materials, to the Si/Gun Committee for examination.
  (3) Where deemed necessary for the examination and decision of the Si/Gun Committee, the competent authority may submit a written opinion on the application for the registration of restoration of ownership or on any objection.

Article 9 (Examination by Si/Gun Committee) (1) In conducting an examination, where deemed necessary, the Si/Gun Committee may, ex officio or upon request of an interested person, conduct an examination of guarantors, inspections, appraisals, or other fact-finding investigations, or order the submission of documents, and may have officials of the competent authority conduct fact-finding investigations.
  (2) With respect to the examination of evidence under paragraph (1), matters not provided for in this Act shall be governed mutatis mutandis by the provisions concerning procedures for examination of evidence under the Civil Procedure Act.

Article 10 (Decision of Si/Gun Committee) (1) A decision of the Si/Gun Committee shall be rendered in writing within 6 months from the date on which the case is referred for examination by the competent authority; provided, where unavoidable circumstances exist, the Si/Gun Committee may, by decision, extend such period by 3 months.
  (2) The written decision under paragraph (1) shall bear the signatures and seals of the chairperson who participated in the decision and not fewer than 2 members designated by the chairperson.
  (3) Upon completing its examination and decision, the Si/Gun Committee shall, without delay, prepare a certified copy of the written decision and serve it upon the competent authority having jurisdiction and interested parties, including the applicant.
  (4) Matters necessary for the methods of examination and decision of the Si/Gun Committee, matters to be stated in written decisions, and other procedures for examination shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Request for re-examination) (1) Any person who has an objection to a decision made by the Si/Gun Committee under Article 10 may file a request for re-examination with the competent Do Committee, through the competent authority having jurisdiction, within 1 month from the date he or she becomes aware of such decision, or within 3 months from the date such decision is made.
  (2) Where a request for re-examination is filed under paragraph (1), the Do Committee shall render a decision on re-examination within 6 months.
  (3) Upon rendering a decision on re-examination under paragraph (2), the Do Committee shall, without delay, prepare a certified copy of the written decision on re-examination and serve it upon the competent authority having jurisdiction, the applicant, and other interested parties.
  (4) The procedures for examination and decision of the Si/Gun Committee shall apply mutatis mutandis to decisions on re-examination by the Do Committee.

Article 12 (Effect of decisions and restoration registration) (1) A decision of the Si/Gun Committee shall become final and conclusive on the day following the expiration of the period under Article 11(1), unless a request for re-examination is filed within such period.
  (2) A decision on re-examination by the Do Committee shall become final and conclusive on the date such decision is made.
  (3) When an owner is confirmed pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2), the competent authority having jurisdiction shall, without delay, restore and register the owner in the land ledger or forest land ledger.

CHAPTER III REGISTRATION OF CHANGE IN NAME OF OWNER AND REPORT OF CADASTRAL MOVEMENT

Article 13 (Registration of change in name of owner) (1) A de facto transferee or heir of unregistered real estate (excluding land not restored by owners) may file an application with the competent authority for registration of a change in the name of the owner by attaching a certificate issued pursuant to Article 19 (hereinafter referred to as “certificate”).
  (2) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the competent authority shall register the change in the name of the owner in accordance with the certificate.

Article 14 (Report of cadastral movement) (1) A de facto transferee or heir of real estate, and a de facto owner of real estate not restored by owners, may file, in his or her own name, a report or application with the competent authority or the head of an Eup/Myeon for changes in land particulars in the cadastral records or for changes in building indications.
  (2) A written guarantee under Article 5 shall be attached to any report or application under paragraph (1).
  (3) A person referred to in paragraph (1) may, upon discovering any error in the registered particulars of the cadastral records, file an application for correction with the competent authority. In such cases, a duplicate of a registration completion certificate or a certified copy of the register under Article 38(4) of the Cadastral Act shall be substituted by the certificate.

CHAPTER IV PRESERVATION OF OWNERSHIP AND TRANSFER REGISTRATION OF REAL ESTATE

Article 15 (Registration of preservation of ownership) (1) The person for whom ownership has been restored and registered under Article 12(3) and the person for whom the name of the owner has been changed and registered under Article 13(2) may file an application for the registration of preservation of ownership in his or her own name after 3 months have elapsed from the date of the restoration of registration or the change of registration, along with a certified copy of the ledger.
  (2) A registrar shall dismiss any application for registration of preservation of ownership filed in violation of paragraph (1). <Amended on Dec. 28, 1998>

Article 16 (Procedures for registration of transfer of ownership) (1) Notwithstanding Article 28 of the Registration of Real Estate Act, a de facto transferee of real estate for which a certificate has been issued under this Act, or his or her agent, may file an application for registration of transfer of ownership by appearing in person at the registry office.
  (2) In filing an application for registration under paragraph (1), the document evidencing the cause of registration under Article 40(1)2 of the Registration of Real Estate Act shall be substituted by the certificate; and the registration completion certificate concerning the right of the obligor for registration under Article 40(1)3 of that Act, the farmland acquisition qualification certificate under Article 8 of the Farmland Act, and a certified copy of resident registration under the Income Tax Act need not be submitted. <Amended on Dec. 13, 1997>
  (3) In filing an application for registration under paragraph (1), a certified copy of the relevant ledger shall be submitted.

Article 17 (Special cases concerning vested property and State or publicly owned real estate) (1) When a de facto transferee of real estate among vested property under Article 2 of the Vested Property Disposal Act (including a person who has inherited from such transferee) files an application for registration of a change in the name of the owner under Article 13(1), he or she shall additionally attach a certificate of facts issued by the head of a tax office.
  (2) When a person intends to obtain a certificate from the competent authority for the purpose of applying for registration of preservation of ownership or registration of transfer of ownership with respect to State or publicly owned real estate, a written guarantee under Article 5 need not be attached.

Article 18 (Subrogated registration) (1) Where necessary for registration of transfer of ownership under this Act, a de facto transferee or heir of real estate may apply for registration of a change in the indication of the real estate or the registered owner, or for registration of transfer of ownership due to inheritance, in lieu of the registered owner or his or her heir.
  (2) In filing an application for registration under paragraph (1), a certificate shall be attached.
  (3) If an application for registration of change in the indication of real estate is filed under paragraph (1), the document under Article 92 of the Registration of Real Estate Act need not be submitted.

Article 19 (Issuance of certificates) (1) When a de facto transferee of unregistered real estate (excluding land not restored by owners), a person who has de facto acquired real estate already registered from the registered owner or his or her heir, or an heir of real estate intends to apply for registration of a change in the name of the owner or registration of transfer of ownership under this Act, he or she shall obtain a certificate issued by the competent authority.
  (2) A person who intends to have a certificate issued under paragraph (1) shall file a written application with the competent authority through the head of an Eup/Myeon, along with a written guarantee signed by at least 3 guarantors under Article 5.
  (3) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (2), the competent authority shall, without delay, make a public announcement of the matters prescribed by Presidential Decree for 3 months on the bulletin boards of the relevant Si/Gun/Eup/Myeon and Ri/Dong offices (including adjacent Ri/Dong under the latter part of Article 5(1)) and publish such announcement at least once in a daily newspaper, and then issue the certificate; provided, no certificate shall be issued with respect to real estate for which an objection is filed during the period of public announcement until the processing of such objection is completed.

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 20 (Reversion to State ownership of unreported land) (1) Land with unrestored ownership registration for which an application for the registration of restoration of ownership has not been filed with the competent authority by December 31, 1991 (including cases where such application cannot be filed due to failure to appoint guarantors under Article 5), land with unrestored ownership registration for which such application has been withdrawn, and land with unrestored ownership registration for which the application has been rejected by a decision or a decision on re-examination by the relevant committee shall, upon expiration of the effective period of this Act (or, in cases under the proviso to Addenda 2, from the date of the decision or decision on re-examination by the relevant committee), be deemed ownerless land and shall be acquired as State property in accordance with the State Property Act; provided, notwithstanding Article 12(4) of the State Property Act, such land may be disposed of by sale from the date of acquisition. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1988; Feb. 4, 2020>
  (2) Notwithstanding Article 43 of the State Property Act, land acquired as State property under paragraph (1) may be sold or leased by means of a private contract. In such cases, the scope of land subject to sale, eligible purchasers, methods of payment, and other details and conditions of such sale or lease shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added on Feb. 4, 2020>

Article 21 (Remuneration for judicial scriveners) The remuneration for judicial scriveners regarding registration under this Act shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 22 (Penalty provisions) (1) Any person who falls under any of the following subparagraphs shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than 1 year but not more than 10 years, or by a fine of not less than 1,000,000 won but not more than 10,000,000 won:
  1. A person who has obtained a certificate under Article 19 by fraud;
  2. A person who forges or alters a certificate referred to in Article 19 for the purpose of uttering such certificate;
  3. A person who has prepared a false written guarantee;
  4. A person who has uttered any document referred to in subparagraphs 1 through 3.
  (2) Where a guarantor who has taken an oath makes a false statement in the course of examination by a committee, the same penalties as those prescribed in paragraph (1) shall apply.
  (3) Any guarantor who, without a good cause, fails to appear before a committee or fails to submit required documents, or who, upon appearance, refuses to take an oath or to testify, shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 1 year or by a fine not exceeding 1 million won.
  (4) A person who prepares, or causes another person to prepare, a false written guarantee due to gross negligence shall be subject to the same penalties as those prescribed in paragraph (3).

ADDENDA <Act No. 3627, Dec. 31, 1982>
(1) (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force after 6 months have elapsed from the date of its promulgation.
(2) (Effective Period) This Act shall remain in force until December 31, 1991, except for Article 20; provided, during the enforcement of this Act, applications for the registration of restoration of ownership filed with the competent authority or a committee and the registration of restoration of ownership under Article 12(3) based thereon may, even after the expiration of the effective period, be examined, decided, and registered pursuant to this Act, and with respect to land restored and registered under Article 12(3) and real estate for which an application for issuance of a certificate has been filed under Article 19, registration or registration of title under this Act may be applied for by obtaining a certified copy of the ledger or a certificate within 2 years after the expiration of the effective period. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1988>
(3) (Transitional Measures) This Act shall continue to apply to persons who have committed offenses under Article 22 during the enforcement of this Act, even after the expiration of the effective period.
(4) (Transitional Measures) Land with unrestored ownership registration at the time this Act enters into force and occupied by the military for the performance of military operations shall be deemed to have been requisitioned by the military under the Requisition Act.
